profile.name: Dr. Natalia Quinete
profile.title: Associate Professor in Department of Chemistry & Biochemistry and the Institute of Environment at Florida International University (FIU)
profile.bio: Dr. Natalia Quinete is a distinguished academic and researcher, recognized for her significant contributions to the fields of environmental analytical chemistry. Her pioneering work focuses on unraveling complex environmental processes and developing innovative solutions for a sustainable future.

location.description: Located at 3000 NE 151st Street, North Miami, FL 33181, the campus provides unique access to marine environments for environmental research.
location.buildingNote: The Marine Science Building houses cutting-edge research facilities and offers proximity to coastal ecosystems for field studies.

profile.labName: Emerging Contaminants of Concern (ECC) Research Laboratory - ECC lab

research.overview: Dr. Quinete's lab is dedicated to advancing environmental science by focusing on critical research areas, supported by cutting-edge analytical methods.

focusAreas.title: Environmental Chemistry
focusAreas.description: Assessing sources, distribution, and fate of persistent organic pollutants in environmental compartments using cutting-edge methodologies.

focusAreas.title: Emerging Contaminants
focusAreas.description: Studying contaminants of emerging concern such as PFAS and phthalates which are ubiquitous, persistent, bioaccumulative, and toxic in the environment.

focusAreas.title: Environmental Health
focusAreas.description: Understanding contaminant load and impacts on humans and animals through advanced analytical techniques (omics approach).

analyticalMethods.title: Analytical Methods Development
analyticalMethods.description: Our research is underpinned by advanced analytical methods based on mass spectrometry, ensuring high accuracy and sensitivity in contaminant detection and quantification:

methods.name: Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (GC-MS)
methods.detail: High-resolution separation and detection of volatile and semi-volatile persistent organic contaminants.

methods.name: Liquid Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (LC-MS)
methods.detail: Targeted and non-targeted analysis (NTA) for comprehensive screening and quantification of emerging contaminants like PFAS.

methods.name: Method Optimization and Validation
methods.detail: Rigorous analytical protocol validation, matrix effect assessment, and standard operating procedures for complex environmental matrices.

categories.name: Aquatic & Water Quality
categories.description: Studies on PFAS in surface water, tap water, atmospheric wet deposition, and marine environments.

categories.name: Analytical Method Development
categories.description: Research focusing on advanced non-targeted analysis for chemical characterization and detection of contaminants.

categories.name: Bioaccumulation & Marine Life
categories.description: Investigations into the presence and effects of contaminants in marine organisms like fish, dolphins, oysters, and penguins.

categories.name: Environmental Contamination
categories.description: Research on pollutants in air, soil, household dust, e-waste, and biosolids.

categories.name: Human Health & Exposure
categories.description: Studies assessing human exposure to environmental contaminants, focusing on vulnerable populations.

teaching.intro: Dr. Quinete is deeply committed to education, fostering the next generation of scientists through comprehensive instruction at both graduate and undergraduate levels. Her courses integrate fundamental chemical principles with advanced analytical techniques and real-world environmental applications.

groupPictures.intro: Our vibrant research group thrives on collaboration and shared passion for environmental analytical chemistry. These photos capture our team's dynamic spirit, showcasing our laboratory work, conference presentations, and time spent together as a unified group.
groupPictures.outro: These images highlight how our diverse backgrounds and expertise fuel innovative solutions to complex environmental challenges. We believe in fostering a supportive and engaging environment for all our members.
